main_result: 45 Trainable rows paired with 135 MOGB component rows; at KIR=.50 Trainable beats MOGB partition+s2c boundary by +4.88/+4.17/+8.42pp OOS F1 while retaining +21.10/+30.03/+33.51pp Known Recall for CLINC/Banking/StackOverflow
decision: "Keep as component-level trade-off evidence; do not call it official MOGB or unconditional SOTA ranking"
notes: Paired bootstrap uses 10,000 resamples and fixed RNG seed 20260725; MOGB rows are Frozen MiniLM fair components with differing representation/partition contracts.

research_question: Do Trainable and Frozen K=1 use comparable score scales, and can radius variability explain the gap to the historical Cascade?

decision: "Keep as score-scale and calibration evidence; never use test oracle threshold as a formal result"
notes: Analysis-only; test score grid is descriptive, no threshold or radius parameter was selected, and no raw text is exported.

research_question: Why does Trainable K=1 retain a better coverage-rejection balance than Frozen and MOGB-style components under the same protocol?
hypothesis: A fair five-seed comparison should show whether OOS F1 gains are accompanied by Known Recall/F1-All losses and whether the result is stable across KIR
main_result: 315 rows, 63 five-seed summaries, 486 paired bootstrap effects and four figures; Trainable K=1 is generally the higher-coverage operating point, while MOGB components reduce false acceptance by rejecting many Known samples
decision: "Keep as protocol-aware mechanism evidence and visualization; do not treat it as an official MOGB or DCLOOS ranking"
notes: Analysis-only; historical fulltex and external-OOS DCLOOS rows are intentionally excluded from fair CSVs.
